_comment: Halden Distribution Ltd. — P9 priority matrix and SLA definitions. Applies to OPS01 GLPI (Setup -> Service levels, priority, business hours calendar and business rules) and to business/p09-sla-policy.md. TTO = time to own, TTR = time to resolve, both in BUSINESS hours on the calendar below. DESIGNED targets only; nothing here has been measured yet.

priorities.name: Critical
priorities.example: Whole site down, ransomware, payroll-day failure

priorities.name: High
priorities.example: A department cannot work, VPN down for all remote users

priorities.name: Medium
priorities.example: One user cannot work, a workaround exists

priorities.name: Low
priorities.example: Service request or a cosmetic issue

business_rules.then: Assign to group L2-SysAdmin with priority P2
business_rules.reason: Security reports must always reach L2, never sit in the L1 queue.

business_rules.when: Requester department is Finance and it is the last working day of the month (payroll)
business_rules.reason: A payroll-day failure is treated as P1 even if it looks like a single-user fault.

business_rules.when: TTR reaches 75% of the SLA for the priority
business_rules.then: Notify group L2-SysAdmin and set status to Escalated
business_rules.reason: Early warning before the SLA is breached.

business_rules.when: Source is the Wazuh integration and severity is High
business_rules.then: Open a ticket in category Security with priority P2, assigned to L2-SysAdmin
business_rules.reason: Every high alert gets an owner (P7).

business_rules.when: Source is the backup heartbeat and the monitor is in a failed state
business_rules.then: Open a ticket in category Backup with priority P2
business_rules.reason: A failed restore test must not be silent (P8).
